We often get asked how you can get involved in the campaign and get us over the finish line in defeating Lauren Boebert. We have good news! We’ve created a few different programs that you can engage with to help spread the word.
Starting with **Eileen’s Crew**! If you’re getting this email, you’ve likely seen the first Eileen’s Crew email that went out yesterday. Our interns are putting together ways to get the community more involved with the campaign. These emails will share with you some meaningful actions you can take like sharing a social media post, signing up to volunteer at an event, or chat with a neighbor.
We also have our new **Coalition Groups** live! Sign up [here](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=2350a8c1b9&e=1c5f08419c) to join our Mom’s for Eileen, Teachers for Eileen, Farmers for Eileen, and a host of others.
Also, if anyone is keen to Host a Meet and Greet, we would love to come see you and your friends, family, and neighbors! That sign up is [here](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=c295bb9dc8&e=1c5f08419c).
And lastly, if you have ideas for events we should attend, groups we should get in front of, or anyone we should connect with, please let us know [here](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=ae02de24b5&e=1c5f08419c).

body:
The Supreme Court of the United States ruled in favor of stripping the Voting Rights Act of a key provision that guaranteed federal and state districts with minority representation. Jim Cr
| | | | | [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XWByNdhdhulCkxGHnQ8FoSumZrWapOT9uv8YnZ5OSQUiLd1-vkTXiAg0W478hwx3WJez5BYvTUjkbx_f0XbecBzJ6u8r-3mSh5S-NmzaavwlJMLaFB5iyH6CKvjLVzwcLRo24XGXyZ5hKIEmgCyGcGtzH2oQC8RwpZneUQXwVxhHlV0p19bK26MhnqtXnIa0QRBUpaqFqKCTSfflheVecX76UoS_2Cvy&c=Jb9TH7jra--HhEuoZAIigv-gNyKyW2D22nWtE6pvns_6kIC7jSZFZw==&ch=tjru6cmQgqyEK5WcQRyqqmXVN4SCiw-U1d3olBeYmaCNaZXUnxAqfQ==)
---
Peter, The Supreme Court of the United States ruled in favor of stripping the Voting Rights Act of a key provision that guaranteed federal and state districts with minority representation.
In one fell swoop, they have given Republican legislatures across the Deep South the go-ahead to eliminate every majority black district. As many as 25 congressional seats as well as hundreds of state legislature seats, are now on the chopping block.
The Voting Rights Act brought about the end of Jim Crow. With this key provision removed, we are one step closer to its return:
---
| [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XWByNdhdhulCkxGHnQ8FoSumZrWapOT9uv8YnZ5OSQUiLd1-vkTXiAg0W478hwx3WJez5BYvTUjkbx_f0XbecBzJ6u8r-3mSh5S-NmzaavwlJMLaFB5iyH6CKvjLVzwcLRo24XGXyZ5hKIEmgCyGcGtzH2oQC8RwpZneUQXwVxhHlV0p19bK26MhnqtXnIa0QRBUpaqFqKCTSfflheVeceUgyXbfLa6C&c=Jb9TH7jra--HhEuoZAIigv-gNyKyW2D22nWtE6pvns_6kIC7jSZFZw==&ch=tjru6cmQgqyEK5WcQRyqqmXVN4SCiw-U1d3olBeYmaCNaZXUnxAqfQ==)
---
The case that spurred this ruling began when a group of MAGA voters in Shreveport, Louisiana, claimed that Louisiana's Congressional maps, which complied with the Voting Rights Act, were "racist against white people."
The extremist GOP super majority in the Louisiana State House and Senate already has new maps ready to go that will eliminate nearly all black representation at the federal and state level. The only thing they were waiting on was this ruling, and now they've got it.
They want to see us go back to Jim Crow and lose our hard-fought representation. In November 2026, we have what could be our last chance to stand against this: the race for Louisiana's US Senate Seat.
My name is Jamie Davis, I'm a farmer and am the Democrat running for US Senate here in Louisiana. My family worked the same Louisiana delta that I farm today, first as slaves and later as sharecroppers. My message to MAGA is simple: we aren't going back.
Momentum is on our side here. The MAGA base is demoralized, and only a fraction of it is projected to vote in November. Louisianans are blaming Trump for rising living and fuel prices, and against all odds in a deep red Louisiana state House district, a Democrat just won by a landslide.
The time to make our last stand and elect Louisiana's first black Senator is now (or it may be never). [Please can you make a donation of whatever you can spare to capitalize on this once-in-a-lifetime moment and fuel our last-ditch effort for fair representation in Louisiana? Nothing is too big or too small - the contributions will add up.](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XWByNdhdhulCkxGHnQ8FoSumZrWapOT9uv8YnZ5OSQUiLd1-vkTXiAg0W478hwx3m-jlZLcP7wNnog2zgGXAhCKDFKO4FWObVzCf01jfNZ1k36E02B_yQMV99ewq3lH3waa8Llki_KmGtwQ9_7DDKC-6yLg6HaaSkGtSMd_TTlYFKYj6J63uyrGfr0QXRvtfqp9NJ68WZGEYGEyPhT4YAX_lI0G-epxUd0c9gWWPnvUuKvgzsMkArA==&c=Jb9TH7jra--HhEuoZAIigv-gNyKyW2D22nWtE6pvns_6kIC7jSZFZw==&ch=tjru6cmQgqyEK5WcQRyqqmXVN4SCiw-U1d3olBeYmaCNaZXUnxAqfQ==)

subject: Celebrating Asian Pacific Islander Heritage Month | May Newsletter
body:
https://www.apipennsylvania.org [https://www.apipennsylvania.org]
Hi Peter,
May is Asian Pacific Islander Heritage Month. When we celebrate API Heritage month, we celebrate our culture, our journeys, our contributions to our communities, and our collective power and pride. We are also taking the time to build a strong API legacy — one that continues to grow our power!
This API Heritage month, we are setting the groundwork to elect candidates to Congress that will be on the frontlines of government, advocating for our needs and standing against threats to our communities. In Philly, we have a pro-Chinatown, anti-genocide fighter in Chris Rabb for Congress running to represent us in Pennsylvania’s 3rd Congressional district. In Central Pennsylvania, we have an opportunity to nominate Justin Douglas for Pennsylvania’s 10th Congressional district, and support someone who has always stood by our local Bhutanese refugee community. At the state level, we have endorsed candidates for State legislature that will be key decision makers on policies that affect our day-to-day lives.
A group selfie in a park where someone is holding up a [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AV001/1/82704/images/05.01.2026%20Rabb%20for%20Congress%20.jpg]
We need your help to get the word out about these candidates. Sign up to phonebank or knock doors with us today to make sure everyone is ready for this election! [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/events/]
IMPORTANT DATES: [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AV001/1/82704/images/2026%20Primary%20Election%20Voter%20Guides.jpg]
* Make sure you’re registered to vote by May 4th , check at apipa.vote/register.
* The last day to request a mail-in or absentee ballot is May 12th. Go to apipa.vote/mail to get started.
* Primary election day is on May 19th! Vote in person or return your mail-in ballot to your local election office by 8 PM.
Questions about voting? Get support in 15 languages by calling 814-426-3542.
This election is too important for our communities to stay on the sidelines. We have to build a country that is welcoming and safe for all, where our tax dollars go towards building up our neighborhoods and our communities — not bankrolling foreign wars and genocide. We can do that by showing up at the ballot box this May!

Our campaign, and I can't tell you how much I HATE to say this, missed our End-of-Month deadline. Lately, I've been doing some reflecting on my grandfather, President John F. Kennedy, and his legacy of hope.
In my run to fight for NY-12 in Congress, and just as a person, that's what I want to focus on. Hope.
My name is Jack, or John Bouvier Kennedy Schlossberg if you want to know the whole thing.
In high school, I spent hours watching my grandfather's speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. When we fight for hope, we're not just doing it for ourselves, we're doing it for each other and the future we all have to share.
I know I have big shoes to fill. In my grandfather's memory, I've led a life of caring about this a lot. I put that care and effort and hope into everything I do.
But this is bigger than me. It's bigger than my family's legacy.
Hope is hard to find in Politics these days, but if we let it die out completely, that's how we really lose. Now cannot be the time to stop caring or turn away. We have to double down in our pursuit of hope.

body:
I can’t stay quiet about this

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. [To unsubscribe from this email list, please click here.](https://act.haleyformi.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?&t=1&akid=2890%2E49239%2EH13qui)

---
null, it’s Haley.

I’m furious.
This week, the Supreme Court dealt a major blow to the Voting Rights Act – one of the most important civil rights laws in American history. **[That’s why I launched an emergency petition to protect voting rights. Will you add your name before midnight?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/17748?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=3&akid=2890%2E49239%2EH13qui)**
| | [Add My Name](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/17748?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=4&akid=2890%2E49239%2EH13qui)
---
Let me be clear: This ruling opens the door for more racial discrimination and more GOP gerrymandering. And as _The New York Times_ put it, “At least one outcome is clear: The decision will improve Republicans’ fortunes ahead of the midterm elections.”
That should alarm all of us.

name: Melissa Chaudhry
subject: You believed first. I'm running again - and I need you.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Melissa Chaudhry for Congress
body:
| Care. Courage. The Constitution.
# Melissa Chaudhry
for Congress · Washington 9th District
---
Dear friend, You believed in this campaign before most people knew what it was. You were there when we ran on **Principled. Experienced. Unbought.** You helped a first-time, grassroots candidate backed by the people — a community-rooted leader, a mother, and the wife and daughter of disabled veterans — make history. You helped our campaign earn more than 90,000 votes in Washington’s 9th District without corporate PAC money, foreign interests, or defense contractor checks — and without selling out the values this campaign was built to defend. I have not forgotten that. And I’m writing to you first because **I’m running again.** This time, our campaign is built around three pillars: **Care. Courage. The Constitution.** That is _the_ test of trustworthy governance. Because people in this district are under real pressure. Families are working hard and still falling behind. Healthcare is too expensive. Rent is too high. Childcare is crushing. Veterans are abandoned in bureaucracy. Immigrants are scapegoated, targeted, abused and deported. Students and workers are told to lower their expectations while billionaires and special interests keep hijacking our government for profit, war, surveillance, and tax breaks. **That is not government of, by, and for the people. That is government captured by the powerful.** And it is exactly why this campaign exists. **Care** — because people need housing they can afford, healthcare they can access, wages they can live on, and a government that remembers human beings are not disposable. **Courage** — because this is not a normal political moment. The federal government is being weaponized against immigrants, students, workers, journalists, vulnerable families, and political opponents. We do not have the luxury of polite helplessness. We need Representatives who will tell the truth, confront abuse of power, and fight like **our rights still matter**. **The Constitution** — because it is the glue that holds us together. A free society does not require fear to function. Government _should_ exist to secure rights, not to select targets. The purpose of power is to ensure everyone can live lives of **dignity, safety, and opportunity.** It's time to remind the powerful of that. You may know what happened to my family. My husband, Zahid Chaudhry — a disabled U.S. military veteran, an immigrant, a father, and a man who has served this country and our communities since the 1990s — was abducted by ICE at his citizenship appointment (which he was owed for _25 years_) and detained for four months. Our two little children were separated from their Baba. Our family lived through the terror of having government power turned against us without due process, without mercy, and without accountability. **We fought back.** We fought in federal court. We fought across four jurisdictions. We fought while exhausted, heartbroken, and under pressure no family should ever have to bear — yet tens of thousands do. **And we _won_.** That is lived experience _no one else in this race has_ — and almost **no one in Congress has**. I know what it means to face a weaponized federal government with my family on the line. I know what it means to keep fighting when the pressure is unbearable. **And I know what it means to win.** So when I say I will **defend due process, stand up to federal abuse, confront corruption, and fight for the people of this district** , I am not asking you to take it on faith. _I have already done it._ What did I learn from that experience? **When you stand up to bullies, they fold.** Some people run for vanity. For privilege. For a title. I am running because I know _exactly_ what the consequences cost when elected leaders are too comfortable, too compromised, or too afraid to defend the people they are supposed to serve. The contrast in this race is clear: **Adam Smith is[funded by powerful foreign interests and war profiteers](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Ff38fbc9e-c751-4530-a25e-3be83e27f6a6%2Fa4393228-079f-4320-ae4a-32ca40e5ed4c%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/1/TLOtX6QBas).** I am funded by We the People. This campaign is still unbought. Still grassroots. Still accountable to you. No corporate PAC money.
No defense contractor money.
No foreign-interest money.
No insider deals. Just people who understand that the stakes are real — and that **courage changes the odds.** Campaigns run on many kinds of contribution: money, time, and public support. Please be involved in whatever way is possible for you. **First: help us open strong financially.** Before filing week, we need to show real strength. Will you make a contribution today — $25, $50, $100, or whatever is meaningful for you — to help launch this campaign with the force this moment requires? [**DONATE NOW**](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2F8e97ec5a-c63b-467b-9bcc-6ee995e18411%2Fa4393228-079f-4320-ae4a-32ca40e5ed4c%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/2/GEWBQ80U05) **Second: give time, if you can.** This campaign will be powered by people talking to people: knocking doors, making calls, hosting gatherings, delivering signs, sharing content, helping at events, and bringing new people into the work. Whatever your bandwidth or skillset, there is a place for you. [**VOLUNTEER**](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Fc8cacc2d-14a9-444d-a88a-a944700a3526%2Fa4393228-079f-4320-ae4a-32ca40e5ed4c%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/3/UOkXCMyZ5p) **Third: make your support public.** A public endorsement from someone who stood with us in 2024 tells new voters, donors, volunteers, and community leaders something important: "Melissa Chaudhry is trusted by the people to be a voice of courage, clarity, and conviction for the marginalized, the ignored, and the targeted: immigrant families, working people, principled activists, and _**everyone**_ who believes in the promise of America." [**ADD YOUR ENDORSEMENT**](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Ff27972b0-2c29-4a6b-88c5-681f1a12f06f%2Fa4393228-079f-4320-ae4a-32ca40e5ed4c%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/4/IEgeMAVkr_) **And ask your favorite politician to endorse my campaign, too !!

** You can also visit the (fully updated) campaign website here:
[www.VoteMelissa4Congress.com](https://track.pstmrk.it/3/www.votemelissa4congress.com%2F/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/5/xqtLDbezup) And **please share on your socials** \- I've made it easy to do so with eight pre-made [share cards](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Ffb0e2c36-dfde-40fb-a15d-6377aa12a371%2Fa4393228-079f-4320-ae4a-32ca40e5ed4c%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/6/OypjkpfTPx) \- you can pick the ones that speak to you. Thank you for believing early. Thank you for helping us build the foundation. Thank you for standing up for peace and justice, for our communities, and for the future our children deserve. **We are not done. We are just getting started.** Let's rock and roll. Melissa Chaudhry

Candidate for Congress, Washington’s 9th District
[www.VoteMelissa4Congress.com](https://track.pstmrk.it/3/www.votemelissa4congress.com%2F/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/5/xqtLDbezup) **Care. Courage. The Constitution.**
Melissa Chaudhry for Congress Paid for by Friends of Melissa Chaudhry for Congress.
You are receiving this email because you signed up to hear from Melissa. We appreciate you, and hope that you will take one more step and share this email with a friend. [Unsubscribe](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Fsubscription%2Fa4393228-079f-4320-ae4a-32ca40e5ed4c%2Fc3146755-460e-4dd0-969c-9be4b5c74717/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/7/FdBuZuEekz) · [votemelissa4congress.com](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/votemelissa4congress.com/lOYfAQ/zBLFAQ/AQ/0a552ed3-fe84-4d7e-8a05-b852e3175b62/8/IltEtKOnc7)

**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Friday!
Thank you to everyone who submitted questions for our governor deep-dive—your input made this possible. The full feature is now [LIVE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) below, along with individual candidate responses published today. We’ll also be breaking it all down in a full overview in this week’s Sunday News Digest.
_**Note from RMV's Editorial Board:** Rocky Mountain Voice does not endorse candidates or give preference to any campaign. Each candidate was given the same opportunity to answer the same reader-submitted questions. __RMV itself was born out of founder Heidi Ganahl’s experience as a candidate, when she saw firsthand how difficult it was to find a truly neutral outlet that would present positions honestly and completely. That’s why everything here is rooted in transparency and truth, with input from the full editorial board._The goal is simple:_ give voters clear, unfiltered information so they can make up their own minds._
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Plus, don't miss our [Tina Peters update](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)/deep-dive video. Here's your summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are advancing major proposals including a bill [allowing lawsuits over conversion therapy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), a [nuclear energy plan](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) that could fast-track development and charge ratepayers for research, and a measure sending voters [a proposal to trade TABOR refunds for limited school funding](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—highlighting ongoing debates over regulation, energy, and spending priorities.

**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Rising costs are pushing even [$100,000 earners into the “lower-middle class,”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as the [2026 governor’s race takes shape](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) with three GOP candidates—though only two engaged with voters—while broader [frustration grows over party leadership](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), spending, and the rise of unaffiliated voters.

**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 to [limit race-based redistricting](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while former FBI official [Dan Bongino says he fears retaliation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after uncovering a sensitive Crossfire Hurricane document, raising new concerns about transparency inside federal agencies.

This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, May 1, 2026.
– Team RMV

Three candidates will appear on Colorado’s Republican primary ballot for governor on June 30. Two of them answered questions from Rocky Mountain Voice this month. One did not.

Bottoms won the top line at assembly with 45 percent of delegate votes. Marx qualified with 39 percent after also filing petition signatures, which lowered his assembly threshold. Kirkmeyer qualified through petition alone, submitting more than 21,000 signatures and skipping the assembly entirely.
The Republican who wins the primary will face either U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet or Attorney General Phil Weiser in November, along with former Republican congressman Greg Lopez, who is running as an independent, and a field of other unaffiliated candidates.

body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260501-2218-foote&t=1001&akid=2218%2E342411%2EZWS6ov ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

Last month, this movement proved something powerful: when people organize
together, we can actually move the country forward.

The Squad Victory Fund is defending our progressive champions —
Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida — and fueling the fights against
Trump’s authoritarianism, corporate power, and the systems that keep too
many people locked out of opportunity.

That means pushing for healthcare that’s actually affordable, protecting
workers’ rights, taking real action on the climate crisis, and advancing
justice on all fronts.

We’re asking you to step into this
fight, Peter.
Grassroots power is what makes it possible to take on entrenched power and
win policies that reflect what working people actually need — not what
billionaires and corporate donors demand.

Nothing about this moment is automatic. Every gain has come from
collective action and the strength of this movement. The far-right is
escalating their attacks, and the stakes keep rising.

But we’ve also seen what’s possible when this movement shows up at scale:
real wins, real protection for communities, and real pressure on power.

That’s why your support here as part of the infrastructure keeps this
movement strong, responsive, and ready to win the fights ahead.

Thanks for being in this with us,

The Squad Victory Fund

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are taking a stand against Trump,
his MAGA cronies, and anyone who stands in the way of justice — but they
can’t do it alone.

subject: Before we get into what's next

body:
I wanted to stop and say this.

| | | | |
---
Peter, I wanted to take a minute to say something I don't say enough. _Thank you._ If you chipped in last month, whether it was $5 or $50, that money is what keeps this campaign running. It's what gets us into every corner of TN-5. Thank you. If you came out to Mule Day, joined us at a backyard gathering, or pulled up a chair at one of the community events we've been hosting across the district, those conversations are the heartbeat of this campaign. Thank you. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/9ejww_dJKbGGh3AyjDI4gA~~/AAUS1hA~/_1wjMkO_eDC8cx33WziCMP4aUaQrMBd44nEAbwt-z5eZxwyCFOxFOIVYhPwd0ahbeo22O4N04nXIa1VRn85jvEG84J3nn9VyvSzVHKI7Gz1IxHE4CD6DwtM8Rp8SYRwqZx7D6lUjQcbEeJ7eXsSgQ2MtGNMJohuXZcJ4TyKKWtoXb_9YPI2EwIJtbVhWwWPgifPSfojfigYuATBvsFUN7r9LQXOivdaWWyZ-u2TIt_W90TfabVxS9_fGKtVAt8zM) If you volunteered your time, knocked on a door, made a phone call, handed someone a flyer, you gave us something we can't buy. Thank you. If you added your name as an endorser, that means more than you know. Every name on that list tells someone else in this district that it's okay to believe in something different. Thank you. And if you're new here, if this is one of the first emails you've gotten from us, welcome. I'm glad you're here. We're building something real in Middle Tennessee, and there's a place for you in it, no matter where you're coming from. April was a month that changed this campaign. The New York Times featured our campaign because we are building more than that — we are building a coalition of people. Our endorsement list grew in ways we didn't expect. And in living rooms and backyards all across Middle Tennessee, I get to sit with people who remind me every single day why I'm doing this. None of that happens without you. So before we get into what's next, and there's a lot coming, I just wanted to stop and say that. Thank you. For all of it. — Chaz

Chaz Molder is the Mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, serving since 2019 and re-elected in 2022. A Columbia native and graduate of the University of Tennessee and the University of Memphis Law School, he returned home to build a career in law and public service. subject: Thank you to the US Supreme Court
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1Cl0xhx5Wyu?e=fa724b03ca&c2id=02d8faed9a08421996be4d5fd2cd9a20)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Family and Friends,

I just released the following press release on yesterday’s Supreme Court ruling on the Racist Gerrymandered Maps of Illinois.

Fairness under the law means every citizen’s vote carries equal weight, not diluted, not dismissed, and not drawn away behind closed doors. If you believe in protecting fair representation and restoring trust in our elections like I do, I’m asking you to stand with me and to chip in today and help me fight for it.
I am running to respresent the voters of the 11th Congressional District, not to represent the government. I will be the Leader this district needs, not a yes man for one party or the other.
Join me in bringing Real Leadership to the 11th Congressional District and to Washington. [Together we can bring real change](https://us.list-manage.com/wPIRS7FSiXr?e=fa724b03ca&c2id=02d8faed9a08421996be4d5fd2cd9a20).
-Jeff WalterIllinois 11th Congresional Candidate

For immediate releaseTuesday, May 1, 2026info@jeffwalterforcongress.com

**Congressional Candidate Jeff Walter Calls for Fair Maps in Illinois Following Supreme Court Decision**
ELBURN, IL — Jeff Walter, Republican nominee for Congress in Illinois' 11th District, issued the following statement on the Supreme Court's 6-3 decision in Louisiana v. Callais:
"The Court got it right. The Constitution doesn't bend for political convenience — and neither should our maps.”
"Now Hakeem Jeffries is openly threatening another mid-decade gerrymander in Illinois. Governor Pritzker should rule it out today. **Voters pick their representatives — representatives don't pick their voters.** ”

"Look at the 11th District. You can't drive across it in a straight line, and you can't explain its shape with a straight face. Springfield drew this map to pick a winner before a single ballot was cast.”
###
_Jeff Walter spent 22 years in the U.S. Navy, retiring as Master Chief. Today he's the Mayor of Elburn — and the Republican nominee taking on Bill Foster to give Illinois' 11th District the representation it's been denied for over a decade._

name: Tammy Baldwin
subject: Why is Wisconsin called the Badger State?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE
body:
| Hard work, and the pride that goes with it, run to the core of Wisconsin's heritage.
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1&akid=5401%2E35263%2E0y4xdS)
Hi Peter — Today is May Day, also known as International Workers' Day. And I thought it would be a great reminder of the strides the labor movement has made here in Wisconsin — and a time to recommit ourselves to the fights ahead. Hard work, and the pride that goes with it, run to the core of Wisconsin's heritage. We're called the Badger State not because of the four-legged mammals, but because of the intrepid workers who moved to Wisconsin to mine. After a long day of work, they would sleep in abandoned mineshafts and makeshift burrows. These ancestors of ours found reward and value in their tireless work, and they built the foundation of this great state I'm proud to represent in the U.S. Senate. And it's not just work that's part of our heritage, but workers' rights as well. Wisconsin is the birthplace of the Labor Movement. Here, we fought and bled for fair treatment, equality, and the recognition of the dignity of hard work. **But that work continues.** More than ever before, workers' rights are under attack. Republicans across the country have teamed up to strip hard-working women and men of the protections they once knew. Attack after attack from right-wing politicians looking to pad their own pockets have made it harder for working people to get ahead. And this isn't just about Wisconsin; this is a national assault on the Labor Movement. It must be stopped. I'm fighting back and pushing to move us forward. From guaranteeing pensions to introducing apprenticeship programs — I'm doing my best for America's working people. But it's going to take all of us speaking out, stepping up, and when push comes to shove, voting. I’m committed to standing up for workers and fighting to make our economy stronger. This May Day, I hope you’ll remember the contributions of American workers and support policies that expand their rights. I know I will. **After all, Wisconsin is where the Labor Movement was born — and I'm sure as heck going to make sure that's not where it dies.** In solidarity, Tammy | [DONATE](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/5475?refcode=AU_STB_CL_GEN_GEN_AC_20260501_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=5401%2E35263%2E0y4xdS)

* * *
The United States has formally brought corruption and drug trafficking conspiracy charges against the current governor of Sinaloa, which is home to the infamous Sinaloa Cartel.

Peter,

Last month, we asked you to send in any questions you had for me, and you
all delivered. I picked out a few to answer today, so I’m going to share
those below. Thanks so much for your submissions. 🙏

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Arlen asked: Do you support a wealth tax?

Yes! My Fair Share Tax Agenda includes taxing billionaire wealth directly.
MAGA billionaires have skirted the rules and evaded taxes for far too
long.

If we simply taxed billionaires, we could fund critical policy goals like
raising teacher pay, expanding Medicare coverage, and abolishing
homelessness.

Christina asked: How do I get a yard sign?

They're in our campaign store — [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1271?t=1004&akid=2097%2E251025%2Ex_-b6E ]linked here!

Eric asked: Why did you decide to run for the Senate?

Honestly, I never planned to be a politician. I planned to be a doctor.
When I was in medical school, I thought the way to fix people's suffering
was one patient at a time.

But I kept running into problems that no prescription could solve.
Unaffordable healthcare, crushing medical debt, poisoned air and water,
the list goes on. These aren't medical failures — they're political ones,
a direct result of a system rigged to serve corporations instead of
working people.

That's why I went into public service. And it's why I'm running for
Senate, because this work isn't done, and it can't be finished from a
doctor's office.

Fern asked: What are your stances on anti-LGBTQ legislation? Will you
protect ALL your constituents?

To answer your second question first: Yes, absolutely.

There are people out there who want to have a debate about whose rights we
give up first. My view is simple: the moment we let one person's rights be
taken away, we've assented to them taking away everyone's rights.

We sink or swim together, and that’s why I’ll never back down when
someone's rights are on the line.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

If any of this resonates with you, I have one ask: [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260501-1-ak.eBM2eP&amount=10&refcode=em20260501-2093&t=1005&akid=2097%2E251025%2Ex_-b6E ]Can you chip in what
you can today to help us keep this campaign moving? I’m the only candidate
in this race who’s never taken corporate PAC money, so every bit of
support helps.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260501-1-ak.eBM2eP&amount=10&refcode=em20260501-2093&t=1024&akid=2097%2E251025%2Ex_-b6E ]Donate $10 ››

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

I grew up in the kind of small town where everybody knew everybody, everybody’s kids played together, and everybody helped when someone was in trouble. We used to gather together as neighbors to celebrate after football games and graduations. More often than not, our gatherings took place at our local public school. My public school was foundational. It was more than my education and the name on my jersey: it was the place our town came to meet. _Heck, the school was the town._ As I’ve visited small towns in other states over the years, I’ve witnessed a similar sentiment. In red districts and blue, I’ve heard about cherished local schools and how they serve as the cornerstones of their communities. But nowadays I’m seeing a disturbing new trend as those cornerstones are starting to crumble: **Local schools are closing after funding cuts, and they’re followed by other foundational pieces of the community.** The local grocery store? Gone. The local clinic? _Gone._ The job with a decent wage? _Gone._ Everyone and everything seems to be packing up and leaving town. We’re losing our neighbors. We’re losing our communities. And we aren't talking to each other anymore. This is what it looks like to defund and divide America, and it’s because of Republicans like Donald Trump and JD Vance, who are willing to sell out our communities and working families for their own political and financial gain. That’s why I’m excited to launch Small Town PAC.** I’m ready to pass the baton and get out on the road to find some teachers, some nurses, some veterans, laborers, and young people in small towns across the country who can represent their communities better than Silicon Valley and corrupt Republicans. name: Melissa Chaudhry
subject: You believed first. I'm running again - and I need you.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Melissa Chaudhry for Congress
body:
| Care. Courage. The Constitution.
# Melissa Chaudhry
for Congress · Washington 9th District
---
Dear friend, You believed in this campaign before most people knew what it was. You were there when we ran on **Principled. Experienced. Unbought.** You helped a first-time, grassroots candidate backed by the people — a community-rooted leader, a mother, and the wife and daughter of disabled veterans — make history. You helped our campaign earn more than 90,000 votes in Washington’s 9th District without corporate PAC money, foreign interests, or defense contractor checks — and without selling out the values this campaign was built to defend. I have not forgotten that. And I’m writing to you first because **I’m running again.** This time, our campaign is built around three pillars: **Care. Courage. The Constitution.** That is _the_ test of trustworthy governance. Because people in this district are under real pressure. Families are working hard and still falling behind. Healthcare is too expensive. Rent is too high. Childcare is crushing. Veterans are abandoned in bureaucracy. Immigrants are scapegoated, targeted, abused and deported. Students and workers are told to lower their expectations while billionaires and special interests keep hijacking our government for profit, war, surveillance, and tax breaks. **That is not government of, by, and for the people. That is government captured by the powerful.** And it is exactly why this campaign exists. **Care** — because people need housing they can afford, healthcare they can access, wages they can live on, and a government that remembers human beings are not disposable. **Courage** — because this is not a normal political moment. The federal government is being weaponized against immigrants, students, workers, journalists, vulnerable families, and political opponents. We do not have the luxury of polite helplessness. We need Representatives who will tell the truth, confront abuse of power, and fight like **our rights still matter**. **The Constitution** — because it is the glue that holds us together. A free society does not require fear to function. Government _should_ exist to secure rights, not to select targets. The purpose of power is to ensure everyone can live lives of **dignity, safety, and opportunity.** It's time to remind the powerful of that. You may know what happened to my family. My husband, Zahid Chaudhry — a disabled U.S. military veteran, an immigrant, a father, and a man who has served this country and our communities since the 1990s — was abducted by ICE at his citizenship appointment (which he was owed for _25 years_) and detained for four months. Our two little children were separated from their Baba. Our family lived through the terror of having government power turned against us without due process, without mercy, and without accountability. **We fought back.** We fought in federal court. We fought across four jurisdictions. We fought while exhausted, heartbroken, and under pressure no family should ever have to bear — yet tens of thousands do. **And we _won_.** That is lived experience _no one else in this race has_ — and almost **no one in Congress has**. I know what it means to face a weaponized federal government with my family on the line. I know what it means to keep fighting when the pressure is unbearable. **And I know what it means to win.** So when I say I will **defend due process, stand up to federal abuse, confront corruption, and fight for the people of this district** , I am not asking you to take it on faith. _I have already done it._ What did I learn from that experience? **When you stand up to bullies, they fold.** Some people run for vanity. For privilege. For a title. I am running because I know _exactly_ what the consequences cost when elected leaders are too comfortable, too compromised, or too afraid to defend the people they are supposed to serve. The contrast in this race is clear: **Adam Smith is[funded by powerful foreign interests and war profiteers](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Ff38fbc9e-c751-4530-a25e-3be83e27f6a6%2Fc5c5a24c-3799-482c-bd59-bd96540d84db%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/1/-SkGpATIuE).** I am funded by We the People. This campaign is still unbought. Still grassroots. Still accountable to you. No corporate PAC money.
No defense contractor money.
No foreign-interest money.
No insider deals. Just people who understand that the stakes are real — and that **courage changes the odds.** Campaigns run on many kinds of contribution: money, time, and public support. Please be involved in whatever way is possible for you. **First: help us open strong financially.** Before filing week, we need to show real strength. Will you make a contribution today — $25, $50, $100, or whatever is meaningful for you — to help launch this campaign with the force this moment requires? [**DONATE NOW**](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2F8e97ec5a-c63b-467b-9bcc-6ee995e18411%2Fc5c5a24c-3799-482c-bd59-bd96540d84db%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/2/r_zQZ8fSld) **Second: give time, if you can.** This campaign will be powered by people talking to people: knocking doors, making calls, hosting gatherings, delivering signs, sharing content, helping at events, and bringing new people into the work. Whatever your bandwidth or skillset, there is a place for you. [**VOLUNTEER**](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Fc8cacc2d-14a9-444d-a88a-a944700a3526%2Fc5c5a24c-3799-482c-bd59-bd96540d84db%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/3/br_C1BWhn5) **Third: make your support public.** A public endorsement from someone who stood with us in 2024 tells new voters, donors, volunteers, and community leaders something important: "Melissa Chaudhry is trusted by the people to be a voice of courage, clarity, and conviction for the marginalized, the ignored, and the targeted: immigrant families, working people, principled activists, and _**everyone**_ who believes in the promise of America." [**ADD YOUR ENDORSEMENT**](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Ff27972b0-2c29-4a6b-88c5-681f1a12f06f%2Fc5c5a24c-3799-482c-bd59-bd96540d84db%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/4/l62RNgCcjP) **And ask your favorite politician to endorse my campaign, too !!

** You can also visit the (fully updated) campaign website here:
[www.VoteMelissa4Congress.com](https://track.pstmrk.it/3/www.votemelissa4congress.com%2F/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/5/wbE9pyxWlO) And **please share on your socials** \- I've made it easy to do so with eight pre-made [share cards](https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/listmonk.haven-server.online%2Flink%2Ffb0e2c36-dfde-40fb-a15d-6377aa12a371%2Fc5c5a24c-3799-482c-bd59-bd96540d84db%2F00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/6/Z_6LtD0cvK) \- you can pick the ones that speak to you. Thank you for believing early. Thank you for helping us build the foundation. Thank you for standing up for peace and justice, for our communities, and for the future our children deserve. **We are not done. We are just getting started.** Let's rock and roll. Melissa Chaudhry

Candidate for Congress, Washington’s 9th District
[www.VoteMelissa4Congress.com](https://track.pstmrk.it/3/www.votemelissa4congress.com%2F/lOYfAQ/JRPFAQ/AQ/955d7f1d-f30c-4e4b-ba6b-44defd4d5350/5/wbE9pyxWlO) **Care. Courage. The Constitution.**
Melissa Chaudhry for Congress Paid for by Friends of Melissa Chaudhry for Congress.
You are receiving this email because you signed up to hear from Melissa. We appreciate you, and hope that you will take one more step and share this email with a friend. U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, at an executive business meeting Thursday voted to advance several bills out of committee, including two of her legislative priorities.

Britt is a lead sponsor of the Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue, GUARD, Act and is a cosponsor of the Federal Carjacking Enforcement Act, legislation to reduce juvenile crime and crack down on carjacking by removing barriers to bringing federal prosecutions. Both bills now head to the floor for a vote before the full Senate.

subject: Heading into a new month ready to organize ✊🏿 ✊🏾 ✊🏽 ✊🏼
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
Condemning SCOTUS for gutting the Voting Rights Act
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/SCOTUS%20vra.jpg]
This week's Supreme Court ruling is a green light for Texas politicians to draw Black and Latino voters out of power. It's a deliberate effort to silence the fastest-growing communities in this state before we can fully exercise the political power we've built. By gutting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, SCOTUS has stripped away the most important legal tool Black and Latino Texans had to fight back against racially discriminatory maps.
This ruling is a gift to Gov. Abbott and Texas AG Paxton, who have spent more than a decade defending racially discriminatory maps, fighting federal oversight of voting rights, and using every lever of state power to weaken the political voice of Black and Latino Texans. With Section 2 gutted, they will move quickly — and aggressively — to entrench minority rule in a state where the majority of voters are people of color.
This is what the dismantling of the Voting Rights Act looks like. When the highest court in the country refuses to stop racial discrimination that’s staring it in the face, it’s telling Black and Latino Texans that their voices and their votes don't matter.
TOP rejects that premise, full stop. And we're not backing down. We will continue organizing in every corner of this state — block by block, door by door — because no court ruling can erase the power of communities fighting for a Texas that works for all of us.
Standing up for workers, our rights, and our communities this May Day
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Houston%20May%20Day%20speaking%202026.jpg]
This International Workers’ Day, TOP staff and members joined forces with our labor allies in Houston and San Antonio to make clear that it’s WORKERS (not arrogant billionaires) who keep this world turning each and every day.
No matter our age, race, gender, income, or ZIP Code, we as Texans know our worth — and we are worth so much more than what this backwards administration would have us believe.
From sinking our economy with tariffs and high gas prices, to purging our federal workforce, Trump and MAGA officials are as anti-worker as they come.
It's up to US to continue to show up and send a message that there is power in numbers, and that through unwavering solidarity, our people-power is unstoppable. Let's keep organizing.
Showing up and building power with statewide partner Ground Game Texas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Ground%20Game%20Texas.jpg]
Building the Texas of our dreams – a state that’s truly rooted in values and puts working people first – requires investment and teamwork.
That’s why we were excited to recently attend Ground Game Texas's latest fundraiser in Austin , as our groups are both pushing our state toward a bolder, more progressive future where ALL Texans have an opportunity to grow and thrive.
Learn more about the great work Ground Game Texas is doing across our state. [https://www.groundgametexas.org/]
TOP Tip: GO VOTE. Saturday is Election Day!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Vote%20flag.jpg]
Don't miss your chance to have your voice heard in local elections taking place in dozens of cities and counties across Texas. Election Day is TOMORROW, Saturday, May 2. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Check this election guide to see what will be on your ballot. [https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/10/texas-2026-local-elections-guide-arlington-school-board-dallas-isd/]
Español
Condenando a la Corte Suprema por desmantelar la Ley de Derechos Electorales
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/SCOTUS%20vra.jpg]
El fallo de la Corte Suprema de esta semana es una luz verde para que los políticos de Texas priven de poder a los votantes negros y latinos. Se trata de un esfuerzo deliberado para silenciar a las comunidades de más rápido crecimiento en este estado antes de que podamos ejercer plenamente el poder político que hemos construido. Al desmantelar la Sección 2 de la Ley de Derechos Electorales, la Corte Suprema ha arrebatado la herramienta legal más importante que tenían los tejanos negros y latinos para defenderse de los mapas electorales racialmente discriminatorios.
Este fallo es un regalo para el gobernador Abbott y el fiscal general de Texas, Paxton, quienes han pasado más de una década defendiendo mapas discriminatorios por motivos raciales, luchando contra la supervisión federal de los derechos electorales y utilizando todas las palancas del poder estatal para debilitar la voz política de los tejanos negros y latinos. Con la Sección 2 desmantelada, actuarán con rapidez —y agresividad— para consolidar el dominio de una minoría en un estado donde la mayoría de los votantes son personas de color.
Así es como se ve el desmantelamiento de la Ley de Derechos Electorales. Cuando el tribunal más alto del país se niega a detener una discriminación racial que tiene ante sus propios ojos, les está diciendo a los tejanos negros y latinos que sus voces y sus votos no importan.
TOP rechaza categóricamente esa premisa. Y no daremos marcha atrás. Seguiremos organizándonos en cada rincón de este estado —cuadra por cuadra, puerta por puerta— porque ningún fallo judicial puede borrar el poder de las comunidades que luchan por un Texas que funcione para todos nosotros.
Defendiendo a los trabajadores nuestros derechos y nuestras comunidades este Primero de Mayo
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Houston%20May%20Day%20speaking%202026.jpg]
En este Día Internacional de los Trabajadores, el personal y los miembros de TOP unieron fuerzas con nuestros aliados sindicales en Houston y San Antonio para dejar claro que son los TRABAJADORES (y no los multimillonarios arrogantes) quienes hacen que este mundo siga girando día tras día.
Sin importar nuestra edad, raza, género, ingresos o código postal, nosotros, como tejanos, conocemos nuestro valor; y valemos mucho más de lo que esta administración retrógrada querría hacernos creer.
Desde hundir nuestra economía con aranceles y altos precios de la gasolina, hasta purgar a nuestra fuerza laboral federal, Trump y los funcionarios del movimiento MAGA son lo más anti-trabajador que existe.
Depende de NOSOTROS seguir haciéndonos presentes y enviar el mensaje de que la unión hace la fuerza, y que, a través de una solidaridad inquebrantable, nuestro poder popular es imparable. Sigamos organizándonos.
Haciendo acto de presencia y construyendo poder junto a nuestro socio estatal, Ground Game Texas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Ground%20Game%20Texas.jpg]
Construir el Texas de nuestros sueños —un estado verdaderamente arraigado en valores y que prioriza a la gente trabajadora— requiere inversión y trabajo en equipo.
Por eso nos entusiasmó asistir recientemente al último evento de recaudación de fondos de Ground Game Texas en Austin , ya que ambos grupos estamos impulsando a nuestro estado hacia un futuro más audaz y progresista, en el que TODOS los tejanos tengan la oportunidad de crecer y prosperar.
Conozca más sobre la gran labor que Ground Game Texas está realizando en todo nuestro estado. [https://www.groundgametexas.org/]
Consejos de TOP: Ve a votar. El sábado es el día de las elecciones.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Vote%20flag.jpg]
No pierda la oportunidad de hacer oír su voz en las elecciones locales que se llevarán a cabo en docenas de ciudades y condados de todo Texas. El día de las elecciones es MAÑANA, sábado 2 de mayo. Las urnas estarán abiertas de 7 a. m. a 7 p. m. Consulte esta guía electoral para ver qué aparecerá en su boleta. [https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/10/texas-2026-local-elections-guide-arlington-school-board-dallas-isd/]

clean_body: [] Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español] Condemning SCOTUS for gutting the Voting Rights Act [] This week's Supreme Court ruling is a green light for Texas politicians to draw Black and Latino voters out of power. It's a deliberate effort to silence the fastest-growing communities in this state before we can fully exercise the political power we've built. By gutting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, SCOTUS has stripped away the most important legal tool Black and Latino Texans had to fight back against racially discriminatory maps. This ruling is a gift to Gov. Abbott and Texas AG Paxton, who have spent more than a decade defending racially discriminatory maps, fighting federal oversight of voting rights, and using every lever of state power to weaken the political voice of Black and Latino Texans. With Section 2 gutted, they will move quickly — and aggressively — to entrench minority rule in a state where the majority of voters are people of color. This is what the dismantling of the Voting Rights Act looks like. When the highest court in the country refuses to stop racial discrimination that’s staring it in the face, it’s telling Black and Latino Texans that their voices and their votes don't matter. TOP rejects that premise, full stop. And we're not backing down. We will continue organizing in every corner of this state — block by block, door by door — because no court ruling can erase the power of communities fighting for a Texas that works for all of us. Standing up for workers, our rights, and our communities this May Day [] This International Workers’ Day, TOP staff and members joined forces with our labor allies in Houston and San Antonio to make clear that it’s WORKERS (not arrogant billionaires) who keep this world turning each and every day. No matter our age, race, gender, income, or ZIP Code, we as Texans know our worth — and we are worth so much more than what this backwards administration would have us believe. From sinking our economy with tariffs and high gas prices, to purging our federal workforce, Trump and MAGA officials are as anti-worker as they come. It's up to US to continue to show up and send a message that there is power in numbers, and that through unwavering solidarity, our people-power is unstoppable. Let's keep organizing. Showing up and building power with statewide partner Ground Game Texas [] Building the Texas of our dreams – a state that’s truly rooted in values and puts working people first – requires investment and teamwork. That’s why we were excited to recently attend Ground Game Texas's latest fundraiser in Austin , as our groups are both pushing our state toward a bolder, more progressive future where ALL Texans have an opportunity to grow and thrive. Learn more about the great work Ground Game Texas is doing across our state. [] TOP Tip: GO VOTE. Saturday is Election Day! [] Don't miss your chance to have your voice heard in local elections taking place in dozens of cities and counties across Texas. Election Day is TOMORROW, Saturday, May 2. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Check this election guide to see what will be on your ballot. [] Español Condenando a la Corte Suprema por desmantelar la Ley de Derechos Electorales [] El fallo de la Corte Suprema de esta semana es una luz verde para que los políticos de Texas priven de poder a los votantes negros y latinos. Se trata de un esfuerzo deliberado para silenciar a las comunidades de más rápido crecimiento en este estado antes de que podamos ejercer plenamente el poder político que hemos construido. Al desmantelar la Sección 2 de la Ley de Derechos Electorales, la Corte Suprema ha arrebatado la herramienta legal más importante que tenían los tejanos negros y latinos para defenderse de los mapas electorales racialmente discriminatorios. Este fallo es un regalo para el gobernador Abbott y el fiscal general de Texas, Paxton, quienes han pasado más de una década defendiendo mapas discriminatorios por motivos raciales, luchando contra la supervisión federal de los derechos electorales y utilizando todas las palancas del poder estatal para debilitar la voz política de los tejanos negros y latinos. Con la Sección 2 desmantelada, actuarán con rapidez —y agresividad— para consolidar el dominio de una minoría en un estado donde la mayoría de los votantes son personas de color. Así es como se ve el desmantelamiento de la Ley de Derechos Electorales. Cuando el tribunal más alto del país se niega a detener una discriminación racial que tiene ante sus propios ojos, les está diciendo a los tejanos negros y latinos que sus voces y sus votos no importan. TOP rechaza categóricamente esa premisa. Y no daremos marcha atrás. Seguiremos organizándonos en cada rincón de este estado —cuadra por cuadra, puerta por puerta— porque ningún fallo judicial puede borrar el poder de las comunidades que luchan por un Texas que funcione para todos nosotros. Defendiendo a los trabajadores nuestros derechos y nuestras comunidades este Primero de Mayo [] En este Día Internacional de los Trabajadores, el personal y los miembros de TOP unieron fuerzas con nuestros aliados sindicales en Houston y San Antonio para dejar claro que son los TRABAJADORES (y no los multimillonarios arrogantes) quienes hacen que este mundo siga girando día tras día. Sin importar nuestra edad, raza, género, ingresos o código postal, nosotros, como tejanos, conocemos nuestro valor; y valemos mucho más de lo que esta administración retrógrada querría hacernos creer. Desde hundir nuestra economía con aranceles y altos precios de la gasolina, hasta purgar a nuestra fuerza laboral federal, Trump y los funcionarios del movimiento MAGA son lo más anti-trabajador que existe. Depende de NOSOTROS seguir haciéndonos presentes y enviar el mensaje de que la unión hace la fuerza, y que, a través de una solidaridad inquebrantable, nuestro poder popular es imparable. Sigamos organizándonos. Haciendo acto de presencia y construyendo poder junto a nuestro socio estatal, Ground Game Texas [] Construir el Texas de nuestros sueños —un estado verdaderamente arraigado en valores y que prioriza a la gente trabajadora— requiere inversión y trabajo en equipo. Por eso nos entusiasmó asistir recientemente al último evento de recaudación de fondos de Ground Game Texas en Austin , ya que ambos grupos estamos impulsando a nuestro estado hacia un futuro más audaz y progresista, en el que TODOS los tejanos tengan la oportunidad de crecer y prosperar. Conozca más sobre la gran labor que Ground Game Texas está realizando en todo nuestro estado. [] Consejos de TOP: Ve a votar. El sábado es el día de las elecciones. [] No pierda la oportunidad de hacer oír su voz en las elecciones locales que se llevarán a cabo en docenas de ciudades y condados de todo Texas. El día de las elecciones es MAÑANA, sábado 2 de mayo. Las urnas estarán abiertas de 7 a. m. a 7 p. m. Consulte esta guía electoral para ver qué aparecerá en su boleta. [] Copyright (C) 2026 Texas Organizing Project. All rights reserved. | | | | | | 🌵 **April Wrap Up** Dear Friends and Neighbors,April has been a productive month at the Capitol as we continue working toward a balanced state budget, meet with community stakeholders, and advance policy discussions important to Arizona families. Here are just a few highlights from the past several weeks.📊 Budget Work ContinuesThroughout April, the House and Senate held joint budget meetings with leadership from both chambers, members of the Appropriations Committees, the House Committee on Ways and Means, and the Senate Committee on Finance.Our shared goal was to craft a balanced budget that conforms to HR1, ensuring Arizonans receive the full benefit of the federal tax cut signed last year. The House voted out the state budget this week. The Senate will meet early next week to do the same. Sadly, the governor walked away from negotiations in March so the House and Senate continued to do the people’s work. This balanced budget puts Arizona hard-working families first by helping Arizonans keep more of their own money.🏛 Policy Engagement & Stakeholder MeetingsThis month included several ongoing policy discussions, including:· Continued stakeholder meetings on our joint social media bill· Ongoing work on an election‐integrity ballot‐referral proposal· Participation in two conference committees, convened when the House and Senate must reconcile differences on amended legislationThese conversations help ensure that legislation is thoroughly vetted and informed by a wide range of perspectives.📚 Free Enterprise SummitI attended the [Common Sense Institute’s (CSI)](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=5f73f38096&e=a7ab36849c) Free Enterprise Summit, hosted by a local think tank that provides research and analysis to help legislators evaluate potential policy proposals. It was a valuable opportunity to hear from experts and discuss ideas shaping Arizona’s economic future. 🏍 Dome Day & Community AdvocacyI enjoyed meeting with motorcycle advocates from around the state at “Dome Day,” where we discussed issues important to Arizona’s riding community, including roadway safety and motorcycle profiling taking place in parts of our state.🎓 Education & ESA Program OversightI attended a demonstration for a potential new vendor for the Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) program as part of ongoing oversight to ensure families receive efficient and reliable service.
💫 Forging a Brighter FutureI had the pleasure of speaking with our legislative interns about my path to public service and the process of developing meaningful legislation.And a big congratulations to a remarkable Thunderbird High School sophomore who achieved perfect scores on both the PSAT and ACT exams — an extraordinary accomplishment worth celebrating. I had the chance to stop by this student’s campus and present him a Certificate of Recognition for an outstanding job well done!🌐 International EngagementThis month a group of legislators met with the new Director General of the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Los Angeles, strengthening Arizona’s relationship with Taiwan’s regional diplomatic and economic mission. TSMC is located just outside of LD2, but a lot of TSMC’ employees’ children attend Deer Valley schools so it was important for me to participate to forge a lasting partnership.📈 Finance Advisory CommitteeOn April 16, the Finance Advisory Committee (FAC) met, receiving updated [economic forecasts](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=ae1e46bc97&e=a7ab36849c) and revenue projections that will help guide our budget decisions. ✈ National Policy DiscussionsLast weekend, I attended the 2026 Club for Growth Spring seminar in Boston, where I joined other conservative leaders from across the country for policy discussions on economic trends and innovation.🐢 No Slowing Down 🐇As we start the month of May, earlier this morning I attended the annual [Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center (SARRC)](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=aee3a4afe3&e=a7ab36849c) breakfast with other community leaders and supporters. SARRC is an Arizona-based nonprofit founded in 1997 that provides a lifetime of support for individuals with autism and their families. This annual breakfast brings together advocates providing hope through countless resources. SARRC offers a variety of programs tailored to different age groups and needs, including services for pre-K through adulthood. SARRC has been such a “game changer” for families all over the world, and it calls Arizona home. If you or a loved one has benefited from the services provided by SARRC, please consider paying it forward to the next generation by making a [donation](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=568b86eb0a&e=a7ab36849c). #HopeHappensHere🗳️ Campaign UpdateWe are gearing up for the July 21st Republican primary. If you’d like to show your support for my candidacy, please request a yard sign [HERE](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=8140748d2e&e=a7ab36849c).Thank you for staying engaged and informed. As always, it is an honor to serve the people of Legislative District 2. If you have questions about any of the items referenced above or would like to share your thoughts on issues before the Legislature, please don’t hesitate to reach out.Warm regards,Shawnna
---
| | **P.S. Having a primary and a general election campaign isn’t cheap. I haven’t had a chance to hold any fundraisers or meet and greets this year due to our constant presence at the Capitol. Please consider making a financial donation to my campaign to keep our momentum going. If you would like to volunteer, **[**please contact me**](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=7c3271b6cf&e=a7ab36849c)**.**
Thank you for your continued support!

name: Doug Lindner, LCV
subject: SCOTUS demolished the Voting Rights Act — we’re mobilizing.
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM2Nzg3ODcS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQ2MDAxNTMzOAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
This week, the Supreme Court demolished the Voting Rights Act in one of the
biggest rollbacks of freedoms for the American people in living memory. The Supreme Court decision in Louisiana vs. Callaiseffectively destroys what was left of the Voting Rights Act to protect against
racist voter suppression and racial gerrymandering, the practice of drawing
congressional districts to dilute voting power in communities of color. This is
a blatant move to disenfranchise Black voters and other voters of color and
further imperil our democracy. LCV organizers are hard at work protecting voting rights, but now we need to
step up our campaign in a major way. The best thing you can do to protect our democracy in the wake of this decision is to renew your LCV membership. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/z9e0fz-wAGB6/blNwb0ZYTTNGN0pTWjBnalQ1NmhES2pDekJVZnJkQlBVRFNUSXpYL2JJYncweXVlMHF5MWNqeXVzMllRZW9kMHlwNDVSYlJNUmZ3UURjbzVQUW1nb1VQMloySGlYQWtOb1RjRGxlQXgwWTg9S0/a0VOUEtmbTFNazc0MlIyWEpBSnN1aWdVTUNYaXZCbmdGMC9GSzMzL2VBYkRyWUZMU1g3VE9tMk5EK1gwVmxKeDBRNWZNKzhjRWJ2OEFsWTU2WXN0ZG9jdGZCNHdVYURCTTA4cWV0VW5SbXc9S0 Donald Trump spent his first term stacking the Supreme Court and other courts
with far-right judges willing to rig our democracy to serve the interests of
corrupt politicians and corporate polluters. Trump knows the majority of the
American people don’t support his dangerous agenda — so when MAGA judges and politicians can’t win fairly, they change the rules. This means we need to work all the harder right nowto defend people, our planet, and our freedom to govern ourselves. This fall’s
midterms will determine who controls Congress for years to come, so it’s crucial
we build up our movement before voters head to the polls in November. Renewing your LCV membership today helps: ✅ Support one of the biggest voter registration efforts in history.
✅ Recruit grassroots organizers in states across the country to protect the
right to vote.
✅ Oppose MAGA legislators’ attempts to rig the midterm elections and the courts

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

It’s May Day, AKA International Workers' Day. While we celebrate the gains
that the labor movement has made throughout history in our country, we
must also point out how those in Congress who are bought and paid for by
corporate and billionaire donors continue to stand in the way of workers
gaining the economic power their labor deserves.

Corporate interests have fueled the attacks on workers’ ability to
organize and form unions, collectively bargain, build power in their
workplaces, and earn a living wage.

The federal minimum wage has been stuck at $7.25 per hour for the last 17
years, while the costs of living and corporate profits have skyrocketed.

Not only that, but many make even less thanks to loopholes that let
employers pay subminimum wages to tipped workers, youth workers, and
workers with disabilities.

It’s utterly unacceptable.

That’s why Justice Democrat Rep. Delia Ramirez just introduced a bill to
raise the minimum wage to $25 an hour and eliminate subminimum wages for
good.

a powerful coalition to introduce the Living Wage for All Act would raise
the minimum wage to $25 per hour for every single worker. It's time
Congress put working families first!

It’s time for Democrats to deliver a livable wage. But the only way we’ll
pass this legislation and get it done is if we send more bold progressives
to Congress to support it.

This May Day, we’re committed to unseating every incumbent backed by

We’ve got 11 more Democratic primary elections this year, which means we

Team, we are outraged.
This week, the Trump-stacked Supreme Court gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which bans racially discriminatory electoral laws and maps.
**By empowering state legislatures across the South to silence voters of color ahead of the midterms, this ruling could hand MAGA Republicans the districts they need to lock in House control for not only November but for a generation.**
Trump and the far-right extremists who will do whatever he asks them to are chipping away at the foundational idea that in a democracy, every voice matters equally.

# [I'm damn proud to be a Michigander](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=196151231&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk2MTUxMjMxLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc2NzY1MzksImV4cCI6MTc4MDI2ODUzOSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.TA3to2yi4TSp_DuHJfiX8kj2t0RnLE3tsj-URLw7K9k)
### And I won't stand by while people trash-talk our state.
May 1
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..699raRpEedxQukyOpGYDlclXpV4AD-V14GBBDZojuRk?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/im-damn-proud-to-be-a-michigander?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Folks,
If you know anything about me, I want you to know that I was born and raised in Michigan, and I'm damn proud of it.
I have pretty thick skin about people making fun of the way I talk or the clothes I wear - because this campaign isn't about me. It's about the amazing people who live in this state. About making sure they have a real champion in the Senate.
What actually ticks me off is someone who wants that job - representing Michiganders - talking crap about us and our state.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d63b01c8-6136-4eac-b1e0-56e44377b2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I love this state. I love what I do. And I love _who_ I do it for.
**[I love everything that makes us Michiganders, from our manufacturing heritage to our lakes and, yep, even our accent.](https://substack.com/redirect/d63b01c8-6136-4eac-b1e0-56e44377b2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
At the end of the day, that's what this campaign - and the work and calling of my life - is about. It's about fighting for Michigan and every single person who calls this state their home.
It's for the autoworkers in Livonia. The small-business owners in Pontiac. The teachers in Grand Rapids, the retirees in Marquette, the nurses in Grand Blanc. It's for the working families busting their tails every day in every corner of Michigan, all hoping to build a future where their kids can thrive.
It's for the Great Lakes, where we learned to swim. The diners in Detroit, where we ate Coney dogs and made memories. The games at Ford Field, summers Up North, and the manufacturers across our state who put America on four wheels.
This campaign is for you, Michigan. It's _always_ been for you.
I've never forgotten where I come from - not when I was working to save the auto industry in the Obama administration, not when I'm sitting at my desk fighting for Michigan in Congress, and certainly not now as I work to earn the honor of being Michigan's next U.S. senator - our state's chief lawmaker and champion.
I know the Michigan way. It's grit. It's hard work. It's about listening to your neighbor, learning from your community, and then leading with the same doggedness that built this state brick by brick.
**[Because that's what it's going to take to win this race. And that's who the people of Michigan deserve to have representing them in the Senate.](https://substack.com/redirect/d63b01c8-6136-4eac-b1e0-56e44377b2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
We've got our work cut out for us, but I'm ready. I know who I'm fighting for.
Michigan. This place. My people.
So thank you - for reading, for believing, and for being part of this journey with me.
If you're with me, I'd be honored if you'd chip in to help keep this grassroots campaign going strong. Truly, I'd be grateful for any amount:
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/d63b01c8-6136-4eac-b1e0-56e44377b2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With love and grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/d63b01c8-6136-4eac-b1e0-56e44377b2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

name: The Democrats
subject: We want to hear from you:
body:
Your voice matters.
---
Derek, **Our country is at a crossroads, and your voice matters now more than ever.** The midterms are underway, and we can’t leave anything to chance. We’ve seen over and over again that when Democrats compete everywhere, we can win anywhere. But to do that, we need your help. The Democratic Party is listening closely to our base as we prepare for elections this year and beyond. We’ve put together a survey to hear directly from our supporters across the country. Your answers will help guide our strategy, messaging, advocacy, and investments in the months ahead. [**Whether you’re a longtime activist, a first-time voter, or somewhere in between, your voice will shape the future of this party and the future of our country. So please take five minutes to make your voice heard and strengthen our movement.**](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260501_supporter_survey?refcode=em_20260501_6957_fr&akid=6957%2E22930333%2ETpmuDY) **[TAKE THE SURVEY](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/20260501_supporter_survey?refcode=em_20260501_6957_fr&akid=6957%2E22930333%2ETpmuDY)** **Your answers won’t just sit in a spreadsheet.** Our team will review them and use the information we gather to help inform our decision-making. Thank you in advance for sharing your input, The Democrats

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

clean_body: This is not a fundraising email | Hi Team, We’ve got two critical opportunities coming up to help elect climate champions in races where conversations with voters could make the difference between winning and losing on Election Day. Whether you can join one phonebank or both, your time will have a real impact. And as a token of our gratitude, anyone who completes at least two phonebank shifts for any of our endorsed candidates this cycle can get a free item from our merch store. (See the PS for more information). Here’s more information on these opportunities: 📞 📞 Heidi Hall has spent her entire career standing up for working families and fighting for bold climate solutions. And with her June 2 primary coming up fast, she needs our voices behind her right now. We’ll hear from Jane and Heidi before we dive in to make calls to voters across the district to make sure they know what’s at stake in this crucial primary election. | 📞 📞 We have the opportunity to elect a true climate champion to the Oregon State Senate this May, but it’s going to be close. Tonia Moro is an attorney and activist who led the successful fight to stop the Jordan Cove LNG export project in southern Oregon. She’s taken on the fossil fuel industry and won. And in the State Senate, she’ll fight to make polluters pay for the fires, floods, and climate damage impacting Oregon communities. The winner of the Democratic primary on May 19 will almost certainly become the next State Senator for District 3, and we expect this race to come down to a very slim margin. A few more conversations with voters could make the difference. These are exactly the kinds of races where people power can tip the scales. If you’ve never phonebanked before, we’ll train you. If you have, we’d love to have you back. Can you join us this week? Thanks so much, \- JanePAC Volunteers P.S. – To claim your free item, reach out to Dan from the JanePAC team at dan@janepac.com after you complete your 2 phonebank shifts for more information. | Follow along: | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. name: Jason Crow
subject: Trump and the GOP don’t care about your health
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jason Crow for Congress
body:
Jason Crow For Colorado [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP21/1/88523/images/Screenshot%202025-08-21%20at%2010.50.41%E2%80%AFAM.png]
Friend,

Growing up in a working class family, I learned early how rising prices hurt working people. When the price of food or gas ticks up, families have to make hard decisions about paying their bills, limiting other expenses, and saving less. All too often, health care is just too expensive, and families are juggling so many other costs.

This is the reality for many hardworking Coloradans.

With Trump and the Republicans in charge, the ability for families to pay their bills and afford health care has gotten harder. Trump has called the affordability crisis a “hoax” and he pushed his Republican allies in Congress to kick millions of Americans off their health care to pay for tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy and an endless war.

Republicans in Congress voted against extending health care tax credits for working families, driving up premiums and prescription drug costs for tens of thousands of Coloradans and millions of Americans across the country. They made the largest cuts to Medicaid in history, leaving millions of people without coverage.

I will keep fighting to make health care more accessible and affordable. That’s just one reason Republicans and their dark money donors are coming after me, and why we need the resources to fight back.

name: Reagan Dunn
subject: Enough is enough—an update from Reagan Dunn.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Reagan Dunn
body:
You deserve accountability. Help me demand it. | | https://us5.forward-to-friend.com/forward?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id;=480818f80a&e;=77eef70c61 | Is this email not displaying correctly?
[View it in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/5279e827759a/we-did-it-10148071?e=77eef70c61).
---|---
| [](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=1d95b13594&e=77eef70c61)
---
| | Friend,

I am reaching out to you with an important update about your taxpayer dollars.
* **Recently** , [a series of reports and investigations](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=5efb203e71&e=77eef70c61) have confirmed serious problems with how public dollars were managed. These investigations stem from my work to demand an Audit of King County DCHS funding years ago.
* **Then** , a joint report by the County Auditor and Ombuds outlined significant financial risks and made recommendations to strengthen King County's financial security.
* **Now** , a forensic review of the King County Regional Homelessness Authority (KCRHA) has uncovered significant financial mismanagement of taxpayer dollars.

_**You deserve accountability. [Help me demand it!](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=1f1e8be75a&e=77eef70c61)**_
Friend, as unacceptable as these findings are, they are unfortunately not a bit surprising. I first pointed out the failures of the KCRHA model all the way back in 2019, and [wrote an Op-Ed](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=e79bbd88c5&e=77eef70c61) in the Seattle Times calling for King County to separate from the failed system years ago.

_Enough is enough._ That's why I've been leading the charge for real reforms to solve each of the problems mentioned above.
* **Recently** , the King County Council unanimously passed my legislation to reform our grant funding processes.
* **Then** , I co-sponsored legislation to create an independent Inspector General Division with the authority to investigate fraud, recover misspent dollars, and finally bring real accountability to county government.
* **Now** , I'm working to pass legislation to pull King County out of the disastrous KCRHA entirely.

This is my focus: identifying waste, demanding accountability, and making sure government actually delivers results for the people paying for it (YOU).

But I can't do this work alone. _I need your help._**Would you be willing to[make a one-time contribution of $25, $35, or even $75](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=512a74e78e&e=77eef70c61) to help me ****_amplify the message_** that taxpayer dollars need to be protected from waste, misuse, and abuse? \--------------------
**[DONATE NOW](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=9ff37ab3a8&e=77eef70c61)**
\-------------------- Friend, your support over the years has meant the world to me, and you inspire me to keep fighting for you!

Thank you!
Reagan Dunn
